headline: Approved issuing up to $3,000,000 in revenue bond anticipation notes for Tidewater Phase 1B project.
summary: The vote approved a resolution to borrow up to $3,000,000 from the Rhode Island Infrastructure Bank through revenue bond anticipation notes. The state agreed to transfer about $9,003,354.58 in incremental economic activity taxes, and about $6,000,000 of that would pay down 2021 notes for the Apex site.
decisions: Approved the note resolution for up to $3,000,000 in Tidewater Phase 1B revenue bond anticipation notes, 3-0.

decision_titles: $3,000,000 Tidewater Phase 1B revenue bond anticipation notes
plain_text:
PRA Meeting 
Meeting Minutes 
September 15, 2026, 10:00 AM 
 
Call to Order  
The meeting was called to order at 10:00 a.m. 
Roll Call  
A quorum was established.  In attendance:  Larry Monastesse, Timothy O’Riley, Mark 
McLaughlin 
Others:  Jason Pezzullo, Timothy Chapman, Karen Grande, Nico Corbo, Jacob Alderman, 
Mary Bourdeau, Irina Gorman- Zoom:  Joshua Glass, Lance Hill 
 
Public Input Session  - None 
Vote: Note Resolution Authorizing the Issuance and Sale of Pawtucket Redevelopment 
Agency (Tidewater Phase 1B Project) Revenue Bond Anticipation Notes in One or More 
Series in an aggregate amount not to exceed $3,000,000 and Addressing Other Matters 
Including the Deposit and Application of Incremental State Economic Activity Taxes  
Ms. Grande presented a detailed overview of the resolution. She provided background on the 
downtown Pawtucket redevelopment statute adopted in 2019 and the Agency's prior issuance 
of two series of Tidewater Stadium bonds. She explained that the State Economic Activity 
Taxes (EATS) agreement, entered into between the Agency and the State some years prior, 
contemplated the Agency's ability to issue "super bonds" — obligations payable not from 
local property taxes, but from incremental state economic activity taxes generated within the 
City's Arts District, Growth District, and Ballpark District. 
Ms. Grande explained that while the State had been turning over baseline taxes to service the 
Tidewater Stadium bonds, it had retained the incremental taxes. Following sustained 
negotiations with the State — particularly since June — the State agreed to transfer 
approximately $9,003,354.58 in accumulated incremental economic activity taxes to the 
Agency's bond trustee, effective the date of the meeting. Additionally, the State agreed to 
remit incremental taxes on a quarterly basis going forward. 
Ms. Grande described the overall plan of finance as follows: 
● $2,000,000 of the $9 million transfer would be applied immediately on a "pay-as-you-
go" basis to fund infrastructure projects already underway with contractors on-site. 
● $3,000,000 would be borrowed from the Rhode Island Infrastructure Bank (RIB) 
under two programs — $1,500,000 under the Municipal Road and Bridge program 
and $1,500,000 under the new Resilient Rhody program — evidenced by the revenue 
bond anticipation notes being authorized by this resolution. 
● Approximately $6,000,000 of the transfer would be applied to pay down a portion of 
the $20,000,000 in bond anticipation notes issued in 2021 for acquisition of the Apex
site, which are coming due in December, thereby reducing the amount to be rolled 
over. 
● The short-term notes are expected to be refinanced with long-term super TIF bonds in 
approximately March of the following year, with a total borrowing contemplated of 
$34,000,000 (inclusive of the initial $3,000,000), repayable over 20 years. 
Ms. Grande emphasized that RIB offers subsidized interest rates — either 0.333% or 0.25% 
below market rates depending on the program — making leveraged borrowing more 
financially advantageous than spending down the economic activity taxes directly. Two 
financial consultants had reviewed the plan: Municap, which prepared a projection of 
estimated economic activity taxes over the next 20 years, and Public Financial Management, 
the Agency's municipal financial adviser, which produced a spreadsheet confirming that 
projected EATS revenues would be sufficient to cover required debt service coverage ratios. 
Fourth Amendment to the EATS Agreement. Ms. Grande highlighted a significant new 
element in the amended State Economic Activity Taxes agreement: a project certification 
process requiring the Agency to submit project information to the Governor's office, which 
then has a limited opportunity for review and follow-up questions. If the Governor's office 
does not respond within the prescribed period, the Agency may proceed. Ms. Grande noted 
that the Agency and its advisers — including engineering and financial consultants — had 
already engaged with the State in connection with the execution of this amendment. 
Ms. Grande walked the board through the key provisions of the resolution, noting that it was 
similar in structure to the note resolution adopted in 2021 for the Apex project. Principal 
provisions included: authorization of the $3,000,000 notes in denominations of $100,000 
(consistent with sophisticated investor requirements); establishment of trust accounts 
including a Pledged Revenues Fund, Project Fund (with a PayGo project account), Debt 
Service Fund, Administrative Fund, and Rebate Fund; authorization of investment 
instructions; direction to the trustee to receive and apply state economic activity taxes; and a 
Certificate of Determination to be signed by the Chair or Vice Chair once final terms and 
interest rates are negotiated with RIB over the coming weeks. 
Ms. Grande also noted a handwritten amendment she proposed to Section 10.12 of the 
resolution to explicitly authorize and approve the Fourth Amendment to the EATS 
Agreement and to ratify and confirm all prior actions taken in connection therewith, which 
she indicated was necessary to support the legal opinions she would be required to render to 
RIB upon note issuance. 
Board member asked why the Agency would borrow $3,000,000 if it had just received 
$9,000,000 from the State. Ms. Grande explained that borrowing at subsidized interest rates 
allows the Agency to leverage funds and finance a greater volume of improvements over time 
than a pay-as-you-go approach would permit — analogous to financing a mortgage rather 
than paying cash. Board members also confirmed that the projected EATS revenues had been 
independently verified as sufficient to cover debt service. 
The Board was further informed that wire instructions had already been transmitted to the 
State, that the trustee accounts were in the process of being established, and that the Chair 
had already signed the order to the trustee to receive and apply the EATS funds. An 
incumbency certificate and investment instructions were also prepared for execution. The 
resolution also authorized a potential depository relationship with Centreville Bank, 
consistent with the Agency's existing banking relationships, though no formal depository 
agreement was being entered into at this time.
Ms. Grande confirmed that the notes would be structured as either tax-exempt or taxable with 
tax-exempt covenants, with the latter approach used where appropriate to protect against IRS 
audit exposure. 
Mr. O’Riley made a motion to approve the Note Resolution Authorizing the Issuance 
and Sale of Pawtucket Redevelopment Agency (Tidewater Phase 1B Project) Revenue 
Bond Anticipation Notes in One or More Series in an aggregate amount not to exceed 
$3,000,000 and Addressing Other Matters Including the Deposit and Application of 
Incremental State Economic Activity Taxes seconded by Mr. McLaughlin. The motion 
carried 3-0. 
Motion to Adjourn  
Mr. McLaughlin made a motion to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Mr. O’Riley.  
Motion passed 3-0.
